newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian interbank rates steady on boosted supply.
newsitem.headline: Croatian interbank rates steady on boosted supply.

text.p: Croatian interbank rates remained steady amid boosted supply on Wednesday as one foreign bank offered kuna at favourable terms, dealers said.
"In the morning it seemed supply would be short, but then one foreign bank offered two-week money at 13 percent," one dealer said and added: "Situation on the market is very good."
She said the money went quickly, and even banks which originally sought no funds took up the offer.
Fresh morning trade was mostly at a two-week 13 percent rate and 10.5 percent for call money.

Overnight trade on Tuesday rose tenfold to a total 121.4 million kuna. Of this one bank sought 100 million to maintain its mandatory reserve and the rest went to three banks with shortfalls. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
